answer_text: The family of the young seagull refuses to treat fear as a reason to stay on the rock. They fly away and will not bring him food, so a day's hunger works on him more strongly than any speech. His mother then performs a calculated kindness: she comes close with a piece of fish and stops where he must leave the ledge to get it. Maddened, he falls, his wings catch the air, and skill appears in the same instant as terror. The others do not abandon him in that moment. They curve and dive around him, screaming, untill he forgets he was ever the coward of the family. The lesson is that support can look like hardness. Without the fast and the bait he would have starved in safety; with thier company afterward he learns that flying is a life to share, not a test to fail alone. Courage here is taught by necessity and then celebrated together.
